description: Invalid JSON.
Schema violation.
File is not in canonical form: rewrite it from the Problems panel or run maquettiste format.
Duplicate id.
File is in the wrong folder or its name does not match the element.
Invalid ULID.
Unsupported model format version.
The .schema folder is out of date.
A second tag vocabulary or category tree in the same scope (global or one domain), or a second verb vocabulary in the project; the ordinally first file is used.
An outputs.allow entry sets commit, which is ignored since 0.5.5; remove it (maquettiste format drops it).
A snapshot archive cannot be imported: not a zip, a path outside the snapshot layout, a size limit, or a missing or unreadable snapshot.json.

A name or placeholder in a batch finds nothing. No element or sub-element of that kind has the name (an update's or delete's target on the model as loaded; any other name on the model as the earlier operations leave it, with the operation's own element as it will be written), or no operation declares the placeholder. A form through an element renamed earlier in the batch keeps the old qualifier: use the id or a second batch. An upsert with an expectedHash, for a name that finds nothing, is one too.

A name in a batch finds more than one element or sub-element. Use a longer form (package, database, schema, owner or seed), or the id when every form is shared; the message lists each candidate's longest form and id. An upsert's name is one too when several elements would have it after the batch.

A write misuses an identity: a placeholder declared twice; as on a delete, a schema, materialize, process or tag operation, or on an object that is not a sub-element; two expectedHashes keys for one element; or an update that drops a sub-element and adds one without an id under the same parent and property with the same name (send the existing id to keep it). An upsert of the same name twice, or one that replaces an existing part with one that has no id, is one too.

A name in a batch is malformed or misplaced: not @kind:path or $name, an unknown kind or one without names, an empty or unclosed quoted segment, a name as a create's id (declare a placeholder with as), or a placeholder where the element must exist before the batch (an update's or delete's id, an expectedHashes key). An upsert's id that is not a qualified name of a whole element other than a seed, is not a name the element will have, or would move the element it finds, is one too.
A JSON Patch cannot be applied: an unknown op, a path or from that does not resolve, an index out of range, a failed test, or a change to id or kind; nothing is written.
A custom kind file is invalid: its type differs from its file name, its properties do not compile as a JSON Schema, or its required names a property it does not declare.
An x-member keyword is misplaced: not true, not on an array whose items is an object schema, on an item schema that declares id, or under an applicator the walk does not follow.
A custom element's type names no custom kind file (extensions/kinds/<type>.json); its content is not checked.
Dangling reference.
Reference to an element of the wrong kind.
Unknown stereotype: a key in a stereotype list, or in a process subject entry's, a named trigger point subject's or a relation end type's stereotype, that names no stereotype.
Stereotype not applicable to this kind.
Unknown category.
Undeclared tag (an error when the tag vocabulary is strict).
Attribute validation names an unknown rule.
A tag or category is declared only in a domain vocabulary outside the element's domain chain.

An x-ref keyword is malformed: an unknown kind or key, a custom:<type> whose type is not a key, of or sameDatabase where they do not fit, an of naming no element (or, under kind member, no custom element), not on a string, under an applicator the link walk does not follow, or beside a patternProperties pattern that needs backtracking (a lookaround, backreference, atomic group or conditional).
A value an x-ref types is a name or other text, not an id.

An x-ref value is out of scope: a member of another element, a member of a custom element other than the one of names, a row of another list, another database, a holder with no single database, or a stereotype default under of "$element" or sameDatabase.
An element carries two stereotypes of one group, own, implied or from a schema or package default.
An element carries a stereotype that requires another it does not carry.
An element carries two stereotypes that conflict.
A stereotype's requires, conflicts or implies names an unknown key or itself, conflicts with one it requires or implies, or implies one of its own group.
A stereotype implies one that implies others; implication is one level.
A property value fails the parameters of a stereotype the element carries (required included, on the merged values), or a default fails its own property schema (required not applied).
A stereotype's parameters is not a valid schema, or its required names an undeclared parameter.

A reference from one package to another that its package does not depend on (dependsOn of the package or a parent). A relation end's entity entries in types count; its stereotype entries and anyEntity reach entities in any package and do not.
dependsOn names the package itself or forms a cycle.
A reference to a retired element or sub-element from one that is not retired (membership, owning references and diagrams excepted).
A stereotype's members do not fit: members on a stereotype whose appliesTo leaves out table, a contributed column with attribute or sequence, or a contributed key, index or check with a name.
A stereotype's key, index or check names a column the stereotype does not declare.

A contributed foreign key's target is invalid: both or neither of referencesTable and referencesParameter; a referencesParameter that is not a required string parameter with x-ref kind table and sameDatabase; or referencesColumns beside referencesParameter.
A redefines entry is invalid: it names a member the element does not inherit, names one twice, states no facet, or states a facet its member's kind does not take.
An excludes entry names a member the element does not inherit or also redefines, or excludes a column that an inherited key, index or check the element keeps uses.
excludeStereotypes names a stereotype the element lists in stereotypes, or one a listed stereotype implies; only defaults can be excluded.
excludeStereotypes names a stereotype no schema or package default gives the element, so it excludes nothing.
A defaultStereotypes list names two stereotypes of one group, or two that conflict.

Duplicate name in scope. A trigger point's name is unique among its lifecycle's trigger points and apart from its process's guards, its libraries' guards included, so a step's assume never names two. An approval's stages each have their own name, and so do its signatures, across its stages.
Inheritance cycle.
Package cycle.
Category cycle.
Entity without a key.
Key names a missing attribute.
Duplicate attribute name, virtual attributes included.
Relation end count does not match its kind.
Navigation collides with a member of the entity.
Invalid cardinality.
Set-null on a required end.
Enum member name or code duplicated, or a flags value that is not a power of two.
Facet invalid for the type.
Custom scalar base is not a built-in type.
Value object containment cycle.
Composition child with two owners. A child end with several types makes each entity it covers a child; an owner end with several types counts as one owner.
Default value looks like a credential.
Invalid name for the element kind.

Literal default does not match its type: an attribute's (use defaultExpression for now, today, new-uuid or new-ulid) or a column's, checked against its resolved length; a json column takes a string of JSON text, and a column with a nativeType is checked for the kind of value only (use defaultSql otherwise).
A stereotype's key cannot change.
A domain vocabulary redeclares a tag key or category name of the global vocabulary or an enclosing domain's.
A diagram with membership 'package' and no package: it has nothing to follow; set the diagram's package, or set membership to 'explicit' so its members list is the diagram.
An operation sets level collection without a subject; the level is ignored.

An operation member is not exactly one of a typed value (type), a record key (keyOf) or a file (file); mediaTypes sits on a member that is not a file; a record key or a file sets default, precision, scale or validation, or a record key sets length; or a member of a returns sets default.
An outcome's returns is not exactly one of members, entity or file; mediaTypes sits beside no file; list sits beside file; paging is set without list; or paging and maxPageSize are not set together.
Two errors of an operation, own and inherited counted, share a name or a code (the code, else the name), or two of its stereotypes give it an error of one id.
An error's input, or a redefinition's input, is not an input member of the operation that holds it; a stereotype's error has none.
defaultOutcome names an outcome of another operation.
A stereotype declares errors but does not apply to operations.
A read operation fires a process event; an event changes state.
requires names the operation itself, one of its own sub-elements, a diagram or a migration fact.
A custom element's content fails its custom kind's schema: a required key missing, an undeclared key, a value of the wrong shape, or a member without an id.

A relation end with several types (types with two or more entries or a stereotype entry, or anyEntity) where it can't be: on an n-ary relation, or anyEntity on a composition's child end; give the end one entity, or list the types the child may be.
A relation end's types lists only one entity, which means the same as entity; write it as entity.

A relation end's types holds an entry another entry already covers: an entity derived from a listed entity, or an entity that carries a listed stereotype; remove the entry. A warning, since carriers change with no edit to the relation.
An expression does not parse, or a node is malformed: an unknown operator or function, a wrong number of operands.

An expression's path names what its site cannot read: an unknown id, a member of another entity or table, a navigation at a check or value site, a to-many navigation, a collection, a member path outside a rule condition, a payload attribute some using event lacks, a context attribute named event, under which a process guard's condition reads the payload, the context or a payload in a right's condition, the context at a trigger point's when, condition or set value, current_actor() or a payload at a named signature's or an approval stage's when, a payload read by a trigger point whose verbs are not all move verbs or own verbs an event of its lifecycle names, or by a named trigger point, which has no lifecycle, a path in a named right's condition that the subjects of a lifecycle using it do not hold (reported at the use), or an overlay's column named like an attribute of its entity, which text reads as the attribute.

An expression's types do not fit: operands of different types, ordering or arithmetic on a type without it, a date with a timestamp, + on a date, date_part of hour or minute on a date, a site result that is not bool, a derived value of another type, a set's value that does not fit its attribute, a type the core does not have (float among them), or an enum member or code against a value of no enum or reference type, or a code the column it is compared with cannot store.

now(), current_actor() or in_state at a check site, a value site or a rule condition, directly or through a constraint (a constraint never reads current_actor() or in_state); only guards, an action's sets, a right's condition and a trigger point's when, condition and sets read the clock, the identity of whoever acts and a lifecycle's state, and a named signature's or an approval stage's when reads the clock and a lifecycle's state. Also old. (a path with old) at any site but a trigger point's, the only sites that read the values before the verb.
A regular expression outside the portable subset.
An expression argument that must be a literal is not: a pattern, a date_part part, round digits, an in list item; or an in list holds null.
An expression site holds both its raw form and a tree, or neither; a process guard is reported only for both, since a guard with neither is a stub.
A file holds an expression as text; renames will not follow it. Convert it to a tree. A named right's condition keeps its text until a lifecycle uses the right, since only its uses give it a scope.
A satisfies names no constraint, misses or adds a parameter, binds one to another type, names a constraint whose condition is not a boolean that types, or constraints cite each other in a cycle.

A binding lists a check that is neither its entity's nor a base's, or one that reads an attribute the binding does not map to its write table or maps to a fixed-length column or to a column that cannot store a code it names, or the binding has no write table.
An operation guard's error is not an error of the operation, or the guard reads the subject of an operation without a record subject.
An expression has more than 512 nodes or nests deeper than 64.
A column check does not read its column, or an entity check does not read its attribute.
An entity check is listed by no binding with a write table, though one of them maps every attribute it reads, so no database enforces it.

An in_state names states of two lifecycles, a state that is not a state (a history or choice state), or a lifecycle that cannot govern the object reached (the entity, a base, a stereotype it carries or a derived entity is none of the lifecycle's subjects), or no object (a process without subjects, or a context attribute named subject, for a lifecycle other than the process's own); or its of is not a to-one path every subject holds. Through a relation end with several types, the lifecycle must be able to govern one entity the end covers. Remove the call.
Identifier longer than the dialect's limit.
Duplicate table name in a schema.
Duplicate column name.
Two mappings for one element in one database.
Foreign key column type does not match the referenced column.
Native type unknown to the dialect map.
Overlay references a missing column key.
Constraint or index names a missing column.

Mapping option invalid for the element: a key, column or option the element, its relation or its tables don't allow; an ends entry that says no way or two ways to point at its end, or a way only a relation with an end of several types takes; constants or an attribute column outside the mapping's designed junctionTable; or a discriminatorValue on an entity outside an inheritance hierarchy that no relation end with several types covers.
View body missing for the database's dialect.
Relation between bound tables names no foreign key or junction end binding, or a designed junction or link table has no ends entry for one of the relation's ends.
An entity lands in no database: no database takes its domain by convention and no mapping names it.
A database lists convention packages that its byConvention setting does not use.
A convention package entry or an entity mapping names a schema that its database does not declare.

A schema operation was refused: the schema is unknown or its name is taken, it still holds tables, views, sequences, convention entries or mappings and no target was given, or it is the default and no other schema becomes the default.
A native type written with quotes or a schema names a type the database defines, which the dialect map cannot check; reported once per type and database with the number of columns that use it.
A routine or SQL object has no body for its database's dialect (and no "*" body), or a database type has neither its structured form nor a definition for the dialect: nothing is created there.
A routine or query parameter, a routine result, or a composite type's field names a type that is neither a built-in type nor a database type of the same database.
A column's native type or a dependsOn entry names a database type or object of another database.
Routines, views, database types and SQL objects depend on each other in a cycle (dependsOn, or a composite type's fields), so no creation order exists.
A query's source (from or a join) is not a table or view of the query's database, or a call names an id that is not a routine of that database: unknown, of another database, or of another kind.
A query declares an alias twice, or a column reference names an alias that no source of the query declares.
A query's column reference names no column of its source (by name, attribute id or column key), or a column name without an alias is ambiguous or unknown.
A query expression or its paging names a parameter the query does not declare.
A select field names an attribute that the query's entity (or the collection's entity) does not have, or names an attribute where no entity is named.
A required attribute of the query's entity is not selected, so the rows leave it at its default.
A query collection names neither a collection attribute nor a to-many navigation of the query's entity, or its nested query selects nothing.
A nested query names an outer alias that no enclosing query declares, or a collection's query names its parent's aliases outside an equality at the top of its where.
A query's sql expression has no text for the database's dialect and no "*" text, so the query cannot be rendered there.
A query's paging names a parameter whose type is not an integer type.
A query comparison's right side has the wrong shape: between takes two values, isNull and isNotNull none, in and notIn a list or one list parameter, the others one value.
A collection's correlation key is neither selected nor grouped by its parent, which is distinct: the hidden key column would change which rows DISTINCT removes.
A select field's value cannot convert to the type of the entity attribute it fills.
A query calls a function whose name is neither an identifier (optionally schema-qualified, name or schema.name) nor a routine id.
A join's condition does not fit its kind: a join other than cross needs on, a cross join takes none.
A query uses a full join on a MySQL database, which has none.
A query uses a right or full join on a SQLite database, which needs SQLite 3.39 or later.
A distinct query orders by an expression that is not in its select list, or by nulls first or last where the dialect emulates them (SQL Server, MySQL).
A list parameter (collection: true) is used other than as the whole right side of in or notIn.

Names of a query collide in generated code or are reserved: two collections with one name, fields, collections or parameters whose names are equal ignoring case or once Pascal-cased, a name starting with mq_, or two queries of a database whose class names are equal once Pascal-cased.
A query's result entity, or a collection's element entity, is abstract.
An operation has fewer than two operands (only - takes one, as a negation).
A literal or a parameter's default does not fit: a number too large to hold, a typed literal whose text is not a decimal number, or a default whose value does not match the parameter's type.
A binding's source is not a table, view or query of its database, or its write table is not a table of its database.

A binding names what it cannot resolve: a field attribute that is neither an attribute of the entity, a value object member nor a to-one relation end the entity holds (endId, endId.type or endId.entityId on an end with several types); a column its source does not have; a listed or soft-delete column of no table it uses; or an attribute or column mapped twice.
A binding that writes maps no field for one of the entity's key attributes, so updates and deletes cannot find their row.
A column of a binding's source or write table is accounted for by nothing: no field maps it, no constant sets it, columns does not list it, and it is not an identity, computed or defaulted column.
A binding's constant names a column its source does not have, so it cannot filter what the binding reads.
A binding that writes has a constant whose column is not in the table it writes, so an insert cannot set it.
An entity has two bindings to one database; an entity has one binding per database.
A binding's constant (or soft-delete value), or a relation mapping's constant, cannot fit its column: the wrong type, too long, out of range, or NULL in a column that is not nullable.
A binding writes a table other than its source, and that table has no column for one of the key fields.
A binding deletes by key from a table without a primary key, or deletes (by key or softly) without a table to write.
An entity mapping element maps an entity to a database where the entity has a binding: the binding wins and the mapping is ignored.

A materialize operation is refused: an entity already bound to the database, a table an entity is already bound to, an entity in an inheritance hierarchy, a name already taken, or an id that is not what the operation takes.

A table, view or sequence asks for a DDL feature its database's dialect does not have, so the DDL leaves it out: a deferrable foreign key (SQL Server, MySQL), ON UPDATE or ON DELETE restrict or set-default (Oracle), set-default (MySQL), index include columns (MySQL, SQLite, Oracle), a partial index (MySQL, Oracle), an index method other than the default outside PostgreSQL (clustered: SQL Server and PostgreSQL), an index expression (SQL Server: the index is left out), a key prefix length outside MySQL, a MySQL index on a text or blob column without one (the index is left out), nullsNotDistinct outside PostgreSQL, a stored computed column (Oracle), identity options (a seed on SQLite, an increment or always on SQLite and MySQL), a clustered primary key outside SQL Server, a routine's volatility or settings on SQL Server, a temporal key (withoutOverlaps, a foreign key's period) an exclusion constraint or partitioning outside PostgreSQL, an index operator class outside PostgreSQL, index storage parameters on MySQL, SQLite and Oracle, a foreign key's onDeleteColumns outside PostgreSQL (the action sets every column of the key), a materialized view outside PostgreSQL and Oracle, WITH CHECK OPTION on SQLite or on a materialized view, or a sequence on SQLite or MySQL; also migration facts outside PostgreSQL (a fact's migration keeps TODO comments where its steps would go, a rekey writes no DDL on any dialect, and no ledger rows are written), index column nulls outside PostgreSQL, a range or multirange column outside PostgreSQL (stored as the dialect's text type), and a run-once SQL object outside PostgreSQL (the scripts leave it out: its guard needs the migration ledger); also a seed cell that names a row whose referenced value the database fills, outside PostgreSQL (written as NULL with a TODO comment); also a check written in the expression language on a database whose dialect is not PostgreSQL (the DDL leaves it out).

A column facet does not fit its type: unicode on a column that is not string or text, fixedLength on a column that is not string or binary, a subtype on a column that is not range or multirange, or a range or multirange column without one.

A stored attribute of a bound entity is mapped by no field of its binding, so the entity reads it from nowhere: an own, inherited or stereotype attribute, or a member of a value object attribute; a collection, a derived attribute that is not stored and a to-one relation end are left out, whatever the binding writes.

A foreign key references columns of a table that are neither its primary key nor one of its unique keys (a unique constraint, or a unique index without a filter except on Oracle): a database accepts a foreign key only to a key.
A foreign key's onDeleteColumns does not fit: its onDelete is not set-null or set-default, or it names a column that is not one of the key's columns, or one twice.

A foreign key's on-delete sets a column that cannot take the value: set-null on a column that is not nullable, or set-default on one that is not nullable and has no default; deleting a referenced row then fails.
A routine's volatility does not fit: a deterministic function that is not immutable, or a volatility on a procedure.
A PostgreSQL security-definer routine does not set search_path, so a caller's schema can shadow what it names.

A storage parameter that reaches nothing or that PostgreSQL would refuse: a PostgreSQL table or index parameter the table or index method does not take (a typo), or a stereotype with storage that does not apply to tables.

A temporal key does not fit what PostgreSQL takes: a key WITHOUT OVERLAPS or a foreign key PERIOD with one column, a period key with an action other than no-action, a period key to a key that is not temporal, or a key without a period to a temporal key.

Partitioning that PostgreSQL refuses: partitions without partitionBy, a partition with neither bounds nor default (or both), a primary or unique key without every partition column, more than one default partition, a default partition of a hash-partitioned table, or a partition name used twice.

The migration ledger's schema (migrations.ledgerSchema) is also a schema of a PostgreSQL database in the model, declared or named by one of its objects: the bookkeeping tables would share it with modeled objects.

Two index or constraint names collide in a namespace the dialect keeps (index and key names in a PostgreSQL schema with its tables, views and sequences; constraint names in a table; the other dialects' namespaces), compared case-insensitively after cutting each name to the identifier limit.
A view, routine or SQL object depends on a SQL object that does not run in every environment it runs in: the dependency's environments must cover the dependent's, and empty means every environment.
A SQL object with environments has phase before: environment scripts run after the schema script and the migrations, so its phase orders it only within its script.
A table gets two primary keys: an inherited one beside its own, its entity's key, or another stereotype's.

A fold into a stereotype is refused: the stereotype does not apply to tables or has no members; a target is not a designed or imported table file, excludes the stereotype or is written by another operation of the batch; or a matched column differs in a type facet, in another facet without `redefine`, or carries annotations its member lacks, or the stereotype would add a member the table lacks without `excludeMissing`.
A redefinition states a facet equal to the value the member inherits, so the table stops following the stereotype for that facet.
A synthesized table inherits a NOT NULL column with no default, identity or generation, which rows written through its entity or relation cannot fill.
A column's `typeRef` is misplaced: it names no enum, reference type or scalar type, it sits on an overlay entry of a projected column, or a reference type's binding fills the column with a field.
A typed column's type or a facet it states cannot hold its type's values: a reference type's codes, an enum's stored values, or a scalar type's base and facets.

A foreign key that includes a column typed by a reference type does not point where the type's rows are: the type has no binding in the column's database, or the key does not pair the column with the code column of the bound table.
A column and an attribute it stores, or that a binding maps to it, state different sensitivities.
A column a binding maps was renamed or retyped since its provenance was recorded, so the attribute may no longer follow it.
A binding's provenance does not describe its source: the source is not a table file, or none of the columns it records belongs to the source.

A map-by-name or resync-binding operation is refused: an entity with no binding to the database, a source it cannot read, columns for more than one entity or naming a column the source lacks, or nothing to map or re-sync.

A migration fact lacks the intent its change needs: a conversion, a data check for a narrowing, a drop's acknowledgement, a backfill's value or data check, a raw step's skipWhen guard; complete it or hold it.
A change since the baseline needs a migration fact and has none: a rename or moved key, a type change that is not a widening, a dropped table, column or sequence, or a column made not null.

An open fact the baseline lacks is stale: the model no longer shows its combined effect (a change made and undone, a pending change reverted or widened back), or a value map's codes were not codes of its type in the baseline model and its names did not change; migration fold removes it.
The after links of a database's open facts form a cycle.
A fact's after link names a fact of another database.

A fact's fields do not fit its type: from equal to to, a conversion or data check with both forms or neither, released without held, a key or object listed twice, a values code listed twice or mapped to itself, an object kind the type does not take, or a value map that maps codes in no column or collection and changes no name, or whose to is also a from.

Two open facts change the same object and neither comes after the other (merged copies changed one object); order them with after or fold them. The object is the fact's object key: a column for a column fact, a table for a table fact; a table drop also changes each of its members.
A fact's SQL text has no entry for the database's dialect and no "*" entry.
The baseline has errors that leave objects unresolved, so changes to them were not checked.
A write changed objects whose elements have errors, so no facts were recorded for them; validate --against checks them.
A fact's after link names a fact that does not exist (folded or removed in another copy); the link is ignored for ordering.
Since the baseline, a kept row's code changed, a former code was added, or a type's name or plural name changed, and no open value-map fact of a database holding the type records it.
An open value-map fact maps away a code that is a live code of its reference type.
A write changed a kept reference row's code, or a reference type's name or plural name, outside the refactor operations, so no value map was recorded.

A relation has an end with several types, and every end has a type it covers placed in a database where no mapping stores the relation (with a junctionTable or an ends entry), so that database stores nothing for it: no table, column or foreign key.
A query field or a query collection names a relation end with several types, a navigation to one, or another end of a relation with such an end; a query can't yet say which type's table it joins.

A relation mapping's storage doesn't fit together: a key that leads to the wrong table, a pointer outside the table that holds its links, entries that give no table to hold them, a referenced column that isn't unique or whose type doesn't match, a type that isn't a target or two types with one code, a code its column can't hold, a key per type at an any-entity end, two mappings that read each other's links, a binding field that maps another column than the mapping names, or a form that waits (a link table per pair of types, column pointers spread over several tables).

A database holds a relation end with several types in a way it can't fully enforce: no foreign key, a key to a shared table, an id alone, a type column or keys per type with no check found, a one-to-one or a link table with no unique found, keys per type in a link table, or a table whose rows nothing tells apart; the message gives the check or unique to copy.

Since the baseline, an entity's type code in a database changed, and a type column there holds codes of a relation with an end of several types; links stored with the old code no longer find their object.
A mapping states how a relation with an end of several types is stored in a database, but names nothing that points at a placed type the relation covers there, so links to it aren't stored.
Property fails its extension schema.
Validation rule or calculation script error.
Validation rule or calculation script exceeded a sandbox limit.
Invalid extension file.
A rule, rows or calculation script declares top-level let or var variables; it keeps no state between calls, so its results are never cached.
A calculated value failed on an object: its function threw, broke a sandbox limit or returned a value that is not JSON.
A calculated value does not fit its schema.
A template, script or rule reads a calculated value that is not declared for the object's kind.
Calculated values read each other in a cycle.
A rule declaration file does not fit declared-rules.json.
Two project rules share an id: a declared rule and another declared rule or a rule script.
A declared rule names what does not exist or does not apply: a kind, a stereotype key, a package id, a path, a calculated value, a link kind, bounds or a message placeholder.
A declared rule selects no object.
A suppression names a rule that cannot be suppressed: MQ1xxx, MQ7012 or MQ5018 to MQ5020.
A suppression names a rule nothing defines or a member the element does not hold, or repeats another entry.
A suppression matched no finding in a whole-model validate.
Invalid pack.json.
Engine version range not satisfied.
Template parse error.
Output path refused.
Duplicate or case-colliding output path.
Render error.
Sandbox limit exceeded.
Formatter failed or its version does not match.
Hand edit.
Protected region lost.
Text outside file blocks in a unit without output.
Non-deterministic builtin used.
Helper name collides with a builtin.
Unit names an unknown formatter.
Script error.
Selector returned an unknown id.
Stale schema snapshot.
A unit's output path cannot stay under an allowed output root or be an allowed file.
Two elements of one unit render the same output path.
A unit's scope (for) is not a known scope.
A unit names a template or companion template that is not in the pack.
A project parameter value fails the pack's parameter schema.
A project parameter value names a parameter the pack does not declare.
A pack file that no unit reaches does not parse.
A preview names an element outside its unit's scope.
A block unit's target file holds its block twice, or a block that is not closed; the file is left alone.
A block unit's target file does not exist and createFile is false; nothing is written (target-missing).
A write against a model snapshot opened read-only; nothing is written (restore the snapshot to change it).
A copy unit's source pattern matches no pack file; the unit is skipped and the pack's other units still render.
A copy unit's token names a parameter the pack does not declare, or one whose value is not a string; the unit is skipped.
A generation filter names a pack the run lacks, a unit no run pack has, or a bare unit id several run packs have.
A run limited by unit or element renders a unit that reads the schema diff; schema snapshots advance only in whole-pack runs.
A generation filter selects no unit and no output; nothing is generated.
A uses entry in pack.json or maquettiste.json names a pack that does not exist or did not load, or a list names one pack twice.
A used pack's version does not satisfy the uses range, or the range does not parse.
A pack's uses names the pack itself or forms a cycle.
A used pack's helper namespace collides with a builtin, a template keyword or variable, or a root helper of a pack that sees it.
A pack has no units, and no pack and no project uses lists it.
A template reads the exports of a pack its pack does not see, or an export template reads its own pack's exports.
Two units of one pack export one name for one element with different values.
An export's each names a member that is not a list of items with ids, or two items share an id.
A unit reads exports that failed to evaluate; it is not rendered.
A pack test case's output differs from its expected tree: a file added, missing or different.
A pack helper test fails: an assertion fails, the test throws or it hits a sandbox limit.

A pack test is malformed: a case without a project or expected/, a case holding templates/, an invalid case.json or one naming a missing case, cases in a pack without units, a test file that does not load or registers anything but tests, or two tests with one name.
Duplicate code in a reference type, across all its seeds.
Two codes of one reference type differ only by case.
A row misses a required field.
A seed cell does not match its column's type or facets.
A seed column names neither a field nor an end of the target, names one twice, or a row has more values than columns.
A collection attribute whose effective reference storage strategy in a database does not support collections.
A storage choice names a strategy the project has not declared.
Storage options fail the strategy's option schema.
A seed cell names a row that does not exist.
Invalid reference type field: code type, field type or reserved field name.
An allowedValues entry on a reference-typed attribute names a code that is not in the type's rows.
The enum lookup-table storage option ('lookup') is retired: convert the enum to a reference type, whose storage strategy then decides the lookup table.
A uuid code is not a UUID in canonical form: 8-4-4-4-12 lowercase hexadecimal digits with hyphens.
A value written into a column typed by an enum or a reference type is not one of its stored values or codes: a table seed cell, the column's literal default, or a binding constant.
A former code is a live code of its type, is listed twice, or does not fit the type's code (type, length, pattern).
A former code's replacedBy names a row that is not a row of its type. A missing row is MQ2001.
A default, allowedValues entry or seed cell names a former code. It replaces MQ3019, MQ7009, MQ7011 and MQ7014 for that value.

A reference-type refactor cannot apply (an unknown or scripted code, a code taken or former, mismatched types, a binding, a missing field, a second refactor of the type in the batch); the message gives the reason.
A seed targets an abstract entity.
A seed key cell is missing, or two rows of one target share a key value.
Required row references form a cycle, so no insert order exists.
A seed has more than 10,000 rows or 5 MB.
A column of an entity seed names a to-many end or a relation end with several types, or a seed holds rows of a relation with an end of several types; seeds can't hold such links yet.
A relation link stated twice: an entity seed has an end column of a relation that also has seeds.
A table seed targets a table that is not a table file of a database, or lists a column or foreign key the table does not have.
A table seed lists an identity, computed, generated or stable id column, whose value the database or the engine gives.
A table seed's cell does not fit its column (type, length, precision or scale, or NULL in a NOT NULL column without a default), or a foreign-key cell does not have the referenced row key's shape.

A foreign key that a table seed or a reference type's binding fills, or a foreign-key cell's natural key, names no row of the referenced table's rows, or one they do not hold in every environment the row is loaded in.
Two rows of one table's seeds share a row key (in environments that overlap), or a table seed's row has the key of a row of a reference type bound to the table.
A table receives rows from the seeds of an entity bound to it and from its own seeds or a reference type bound to it: a row should have one source.
A table seed has no row key (the unique constraint it names does not exist, or the table has no primary key), or a row lacks a key cell.
A seed's rows file or rows script is missing or cannot be read, or the seed has rows of its own beside it.
A reference type's binding names a table that is not a table file of its database, or the type has two bindings to one database.
A reference type's binding maps a field or a constant wrongly: no code column, an unknown field or column, a column filled twice or by the database, or a column the field does not fit.

A reference type's binding has no key: no primary key or unique constraint of its table is made of the code column (and constant columns), or another type bound to the table has the same constants or puts rows of the same key there.
A reference type's binding fills no value for a NOT NULL column of its table that has no default.
Two seeds of one table key their rows differently (a different key, or a key beside the primary key).
`stableId` is set on a column that is not of type `uuid`, or whose value the database fills (identity, sequence, generated, computed).
The row key of a table with a stable id column holds that column, or a value the database fills directly or through a foreign-key entry, so the stable id cannot be derived.

A table seed's column entry names a foreign key that is not its target's, is listed beside one of that key's own columns, references a table that has no rows in the model, or the seed's row key holds part of the entry's columns.
A seed's rows script fails: it does not load, registers anything but rows exactly once, throws, exceeds a sandbox limit, or returns something that is not an array of row objects.
A scripted row has a key its seed's columns do not name, or the seed's target has no row key to derive row ids from.
Invalid localization settings: a locale that is not BCP 47, a default not in the locales, a fallback naming an undeclared locale, a fallback cycle, or a required node kind that does not exist.
A locale folder for an undeclared locale or for the default locale; its files are not loaded.
An orphan translation: its id is not a localizable node of the model, or it has a field the node does not have.
A locale is incomplete in a shard: the counts of missing and stale texts, for the required kinds.
A missing translation, one per node and field (off unless validation.rules gives it a severity).
Stale translations in a shard: made from a default text that has changed since.
A translation entry in the wrong shard (its node moved); it still applies.
A translated description's Markdown sidecar does not exist.
One id in two shards of one locale; the ordinally first path applies.
A shard whose locale differs from its folder, or whose scope differs from its path; it applies to its declared locale and scope.
A plural name on a to-one relation end, or its translation; it is never read.

x-translatable is not on a top-level string property of an extension file or stereotype parameters, or of a custom kind's content or member items whose name is an identifier: nested, on another type, or not a boolean.
x-translatable is on a property whose schema applies only to kinds without translations (physical objects, mappings, diagrams, vocabulary containers).
A branding color that is not a hex color (#rrggbb or #rgb).
The branding icon is not an .svg or .png file under branding/ in the model folder, or the file does not exist.
The branding icon is not a safe SVG (scripts, event handlers, external references) or a PNG of at most 512 KB.

A trigger point's shape is wrong: timing missing on an action, or beside a check or a replace; severity beside a type other than check; condition on an action or a replace; sets on a check; outside on a point with no team code (a check with a condition, or an action or a replace with sets); a with-change action with sets on delete that no replace on delete covers for every entity it covers; or trigger points on an orchestration or a library, which only lifecycles hold. A named trigger point's body follows the same rules. Remove the key.

A trigger point's narrowing key does not fit: states or targets that are not states of its lifecycle; transitions that are not its transitions; targets or transitions beside a verb that is not a move verb, sign, an own verb an event of its lifecycle names, or, in a lifecycle with an approval, reject, ignore or withdraw, and delegate where one of its signatures has delegateTo; attributes beside a verb other than read and modify, or beside ends; ends beside a verb that cannot act on a link (any but connect, disconnect, read, modify, freeze and thaw); attributes, ends or set attributes that not every entity it covers holds under one id; or entities its lifecycle does not govern. On a named trigger point: states, targets or transitions, which belong to one lifecycle; entities its subjects do not cover; or exceptEntities that no subject covers. Remove the entry.

A replace on a verb that does not allow it: only delete, disconnect, copy and revise do. Moves, signatures, tasks, freeze, thaw, lock, unlock, change-owner, change-type, change-lifecycle, read, modify and own verbs never do. Make it an action.

Two replaces can apply to one verb on one entity: in one lifecycle, across the lifecycles that govern it, or in named trigger points that cover it, beside each other or beside a lifecycle's. Their states and when are not considered, since whether both can hold is not known before a run. Narrow one with entities, or a named one with exceptEntities.
An after-commit action has sets: once the change is saved, setting the object would be a new change. Make it a with-change action.
A with-change action reaches outside systems (outside): a rollback cannot undo the outside call. Make it after commit.

A trigger point that can never run: a move verb that no event or transition of its lifecycle names, transitions none of which moves with its verb, or only verbs no input can do yet (override, set-state, claim, route, delegate unless a named signature of its lifecycle has delegateTo, and reject, ignore and withdraw unless its lifecycle has an approval) that no event names. A named trigger point can do reject, ignore and withdraw when a lifecycle that governs an entity it covers has an approval, and delegate when such a lifecycle has a named signature with delegateTo. Remove it.

An approval's shape is wrong: a gate with stages that also has required, signers, requiredActors or allowRepeatSigner, which its named signatures carry; or allowSignerAcrossSignatures on a gate without stages. Remove the key.

A named signature's or an approval stage's key does not fit: a notBy transition that is not a transition of its lifecycle; a notBy transition in a gate policy, which belongs to no single lifecycle; a notBy verb its lifecycle's runs cannot see (only move verbs, signature verbs, complete and verbs its events name); or a when on a gate policy's signature or stage, which has no subject to read. Remove the entry or key.
An approval's stages are not listed in round order: a stage's round is lower than the round of a stage before it. Stages run round by round, so the file reads from top to bottom. Reorder the stages.

A named signature's reminder or escalation is malformed: escalateTo without escalateAfter, or escalateAfter without escalateTo; or a remindAfter or escalateAfter that is not a positive ISO 8601 duration, read as an after transition's delay is. Add or remove the key, or fix the duration.
A named signature's escalation falls due no later than its reminder: escalateAfter is not longer than remindAfter, so the reminder never comes first. Lengthen escalateAfter, or shorten remindAfter.
A compound state (or the process) whose initial is not one of its direct children, or an initial on a state that is not compound; set initial to a direct child, or remove it to use the first child.
A state's type contradicts its children: an atomic, final, history or choice state with children, or a compound or parallel state without; change the type or move the children.
An unreachable state: no path from the initial state through transitions, history defaults or invoke completions enters it (guards are ignored); add a transition to it or remove it.
A dead end: a reachable atomic state with no transition on itself or an ancestor and no invoke; add a transition or make it final.
No final state is reachable, so the process never completes (normal for some lifecycles); add a final state and a transition to it if instances should end.
Overlapping transitions for one source and trigger: a transition after an unguarded one, or a guard tested twice, never fires; guard the earlier transition or remove the later one.
Invalid targets: a state of another process, two targets in one region, or several targets not in orthogonal regions of one parallel ancestor; keep one target per region of this process.

Trigger fields inconsistent: an event trigger without an event, an after trigger without a positive ISO 8601 duration, done on a state that cannot complete, an invoke trigger naming no invoke of the source, or a field of another trigger; fix the trigger or its field.
A cycle of unguarded eventless transitions: the macrostep would never end; guard one of the transitions or give it an event.
A choice state whose outgoing transitions are not all always, whose last transition is guarded (no default), or that has none; make them always transitions ending with an unguarded one.
A history state outside a compound parent, or a default target that is not a descendant of its parent; move the history state into a compound state or pick a default inside it.
A final state that is the source of transitions or invokes work; remove them, or make the state atomic.
A declared event, guard, action or invoke that nothing uses (an invoke is used by an invoke-done or invoke-error transition; a library's guard, action or gate by any process); use it or remove it.
A reference to a state, event, guard, action or invoke of another process that is not a library's guard or action; declare it in this process, or move it to a library.
Invokes: a sub-process invoke cycle, a process invoke without a process, or a human task without actors; break the cycle, set the process, or list the actors.
A process diagram member that is not a state of the diagram's process; remove the member.
A parallel state with one region; add a region or make the state compound.
A done transition whose source has no reachable final state (in every region, for a parallel source), so it never fires; add a reachable final child or change the trigger.

A process operation (sync-enum, sync-codes, set-lifecycle, set-initial, refresh-scenario, use-subjects) was refused: its element is not what the operation needs, the target is not a direct child or a process, the entity is not the subject it needs, the attribute cannot hold a state, a state code names no state that rests, the enum sync would remove members still in use, a scenario cannot be replayed to its last step, or another operation of the batch writes the process, enum or scenario it changes; fix the operation or the step, change the uses to a remaining member, or run it in a batch of its own.

A library holds what only a running process has (states, an initial state, transitions, context, events, a subject, a bound attribute, an action that raises events or sets the object's data, or a guard with a condition), or a process that is not a library has no states or lists gates of its own; move the item, or change use.
A transition sets both gate and gatePolicy, or its gatePolicy names a gate that no library holds; keep one, or point at a library's gate.
A process invoke or a scenario names a library, which has no states to run; name a running process.

A gate, or a named signature of an approval, needs more signatures than its signers can give (only person actors, repeat signing off); or an approval needs more different people than its signatures' signers can give, without allowSignerAcrossSignatures; lower required, add signers, or allow repeat signers.
A gate's or a named signature's required actors are not all among its signers (a required actor that is a member, at any depth, of a signer counts as among them); add them to signers.
A gate or gate policy on a transition whose trigger is not event, or two of them on one source and event; move the gate to an event transition or keep one gate.
A gate without meanings; add at least one meaning that says what a signature means.

A gate signer, or a signer of one of its named signatures, that may not raise the gate's event (the event lists its actors and leaves the signer out, and the signer is not a member of one of them at any depth); add the signer to the event's actors. Never reported when the signer or one of the event's actors is an actor from the object, which only the object decides.

An actor no process or right references (event actors, gate signers, a named signature's signers, required actors, delegateTo or escalateTo, human tasks, a right's actors or except), directly, through a member at any depth, through an actor it is a member of at any depth, or as the membersOf of an actor from the object; use it in a process or remove it.

Lifecycle inconsistent: a lifecycle without a subject, an empty subjects list or an entity or stereotype listed twice, a one-subject form subject whose lifecycle does not name the process, or an entity whose lifecycle names an orchestration or a lifecycle that does not govern it (it, a base, or a stereotype it or a base carries is not listed); list the entity in the lifecycle's subjects, or set lifecycle on the entity to a lifecycle that governs it.

A bound attribute that is not a single-valued attribute of the subject (own, inherited or from a stereotype; on a stereotype entry, the stereotype's own) typed by an enum, a reference type or a plain status (string, text, int16, int32 or int64, directly or through a scalar type), one set on an orchestration, or one attribute that two lifecycles bind for an entity or a stereotype both list; bind another attribute of the subject.
Enum drift: the bound enum's members differ from the lifecycle's root-level states (missing, extra or out of order); sync the enum from the process.
The bound enum is used by other attributes or processes than the lifecycle's own subjects, so syncing it from the process changes them too; give the lifecycle its own enum if they should not follow.
The bound attribute's default is not where the lifecycle starts: for an enum binding the initial root-level state's name, for any other binding the initial state's code; set the default to it.

State codes clash: two states share a code (1 and "1" are one code), codes mix strings and integers, a history or choice state has a code, or, under a binding, two coded states sit on one path or a coded state sits in a parallel region; give each state that rests its own code, all strings or all integers, at most one per configuration.

A state code does not fit its binding: under an enum binding it is not its member's key, integer value or name (or the state is not at the root); under a reference type it is not a live code of the type; under a plain status it does not fit the attribute's type, length, pattern or allowedValues; write a code that fits.

Once the lifecycle has codes, values a binding can hold that no state's code covers: the bound attribute's allowedValues, else the reference type's rows; add a state with each code, or narrow allowedValues.
The deprecated one-subject form: a process names its subject with subject and boundAttribute; list it in subjects instead.

Under a reference-type or plain binding, reachable states that a configuration rests in have no code, so the bound attribute has no value for them; one finding per binding names them. An enum binding needs no codes, since the member is the value. Give each state a code, or run Sync codes.

A subject entry of a process or a named trigger point, or an entry of a relation end's types, names a stereotype that does not apply to entities (its appliesTo leaves out entity), so no entity can carry it; name a stereotype entities carry, or an entity.

A scenario step is refused while expect.accepted is true (no transition, a guard false, an actor not allowed, a right or a lifecycle's default that denies, a gate refusal, a trigger point's check), or accepted while it is false; a refusal by actor names the step's participant and what it failed (the list it satisfies none of, or the list that does not accept the actor it acted as); fix the step's input or set accepted to what the process does.
The active states after a scenario step differ from expect.states; fix the chart or update the expectations from a replay.
The context attributes a scenario step changed differ from expect.context; fix the actions or update the expectations from a replay.
Whether the process is final after the scenario's last step differs from outcome; fix the steps or update the expectations from a replay.

A scenario step's fields are inconsistent: an event the process does not declare, a time step without a positive duration, an invoke that is not pending, or a payload value that is not an attribute of the event or does not fit its type; or a scenario object is inconsistent: a value that does not fit its attribute, a subject whose entity is not a process subject (listed, derived from one, or carrying a listed stereotype), or a link whose end does not fit (through a relation end with several types, the target's entity must be one the end covers) or that is frozen on an object other than the subject, or an owner beside its subject's owner field or that is not one of the scenario's participants, or states that name a state of a lifecycle that cannot govern the object, two states of one lifecycle that cannot be active together, the subject's state in the process the scenario runs, or a state that disagrees with the state the object's bound value maps to; or a participant is inconsistent: an actor that is a role, group, organization or actor from the object, a holding that is not a plain role, group or organization, a within or object that is not one of the scenario's objects, or a step's participant that is not the scenario's or its actor that the participant does not satisfy; or a verb step is inconsistent: no verb, a verb that is not an object, link or own verb (a move, signature or task verb), values beside a verb other than modify and create or beside an end, attributes beside a verb other than read, a values attribute a set could not set or a value that does not fit its type, an end that is not the subject's, an object not linked through it (except for connect), a connect through a relation end with several types to an object whose entity the end does not cover, or delete on a link; or an assume word (pass, warning or error) whose key is not a check the team writes of a lifecycle the step reaches, or that names a check with a condition (true and false, for guards, are not checked); or a response or signature on a step that is not an event step gated by an approval, a signature of another gate, or an expect.signatures key that is not a signature of the approval the step answers; or a delegation that does not fit: delegateTo without response delegate, delegate without delegateTo, delegate or onBehalfOf on an approval none of whose signatures has delegateTo or naming a signature without it, or delegate with onBehalfOf, since a delegation can't be passed on; or expect.refusal or expect.refusedBy beside accepted true; fix the step, the object or the participant.
A guard without an expression is evaluated during a scenario step that has no assume value for it, so the replay stops there; add the guard to the step's assume, or give the guard an expression.
The values of the object a scenario step set differ from expect.values; fix the actions' sets or update the expectations from a replay.

A refused scenario step's refusal or refusing element differs from expect.refusal or expect.refusedBy (the checks run in a fixed order, and the first that fails names both; an approval adds gate-excluded and gate-not-signed); fix the step, the chart, the approval, the rights or the trigger points, or update the expectations from a replay.

A scenario step is refused as frozen because an earlier step froze the subject or the link (an event that names freeze, or a freeze verb step), and the step does not expect refusal frozen: an accepted freeze takes effect, so modify, connect, disconnect and delete are refused until a thaw. The finding names the step that froze it; thaw in between, or expect the refusal (update the expectations from a replay).

The checks that warned, or the trigger points that ran, in a scenario step differ from expect.checkWarnings or expect.triggerPoints (exactly those ids; trigger points in run order, repeats included, skipped ones left out); fix the trigger points or update the expectations from a replay.

The signatures counted after a scenario step differ from expect.signatures (only the listed named signatures are compared), or the reminders and escalations due at it differ from expect.notices (compared as a set of signature and kind); fix the approval or the steps, or update the expectations from a replay.

XState configuration the model has no place for (custom actor logic, tags, output, systemId, parameterized guards or actions, spawn, sendTo, unknown keys) was kept as opaque data in the process's source extensions and is written back on export; model it with process features where one exists, or leave it for the host.

An inline function in the XState configuration (a guard, action, delay or invoke source given as function text) became a named stub whose description holds the text, which never runs; give the stub an expression or implement its handler.

The import input is not a statechart configuration the importer accepts (invalid JSON, no states, a target or initial state that does not resolve, a parallel root, or an unknown state type); fix the configuration and import it again.

An XState feature was mapped approximately or dropped on import or export (a guard combinator, a named delay without a value, an actor or custom state id the model does not know, a name that is not an identifier, data that no longer has a place); review the imported process.

An id carried in the configuration names an element of another kind or of another process, or is used twice, so the node got a new id; re-import into the process the ids belong to, or remove the stale ids.

Export wrote model data with no XState equivalent (ids, display names, types, gates, durations, invoke kinds) into meta.maquettiste, so an import restores it; keep the meta entries when editing the configuration by hand.
A guard or action expression does not parse as one JavaScript expression; fix its syntax (an action returns an object literal in parentheses).
A guard or action expression threw while a scenario replayed or a simulation ran; fix the expression, for example guard against missing values.
A guard or action expression exceeded the sandbox deadline (50 ms) or statement limit (100,000); simplify it, or leave the expression empty and implement the handler.
A guard returned a value that is not a boolean, which counts as false; make the expression return true or false.

An action's result names an attribute the context does not declare, or a value that does not fit the attribute's type, and the entry is ignored; return only context attribute names with values of their types.
Two guarded transitions of one source and trigger were enabled at once, and the first in priority order was taken; make the guards exclusive or reorder the transitions.
A macrostep ran more than 1,000 microsteps (an eventless loop whose guards keep holding, or internal events that keep raising each other); break the loop with a guard that turns false.
A memberOf entry that does not name a role, group or organization, names an actor from the object (relative), names the actor itself, or is listed twice; remove the entry.
Memberships form a cycle (an actor is, through memberOf, a member of itself); the message names the cycle. Remove one of its memberships.

An actor's relative is malformed: no form or more than one (owner, path, membersOf), within without membersOf, membersOf naming something other than a role, group or organization that is not itself an actor from the object, memberOf on an actor from the object, or type system with relative; give exactly one form.

An actor from the object is used where it cannot be worked out: in a process with no subjects, or with a path (or within) that does not resolve on every subject (the subject's own and inherited members and the attributes of the stereotypes it or a base carries for one subject, what every subject holds under one id for several; a stereotype entry holds its stereotype's own attributes and no relation ends, so with one a path is one step to such an attribute and within is empty), that passes through something other than a to-one relation end (beyond an end with several types, a path reads what every entity the end covers holds under one id), or that ends at a many-valued attribute, a value object or a to-many end. Reported at the use; a library's gate or human task at each process that uses it, a named right's actors and except at each lifecycle that uses it.
Two or more actors of type system: the system itself (shown as Automatic) is one actor per project; change the type of all but one, for example to external-system, or give it roles through memberOf.

A subject entry's owner that is not a single-valued attribute or a to-one relation end of its entity (own or inherited, or an attribute of a stereotype the entity or a base carries), or on a stereotype entry a single-valued attribute of the stereotype's own; clear the owner, or name a field that holds one actor.

A verb that is neither a built-in verb nor one of the project's own (model/vocabularies/verbs.json). Reported at the event, transition, operation, right, trigger point or named signature's notBy; add it to the project's verbs, or clear it.

An own verb whose key is a built-in verb's, or two own verbs with one key, also once hyphens are dropped (x-1 and x1); use the built-in verb (rename-verb to it), merge the two, or give the verb another key.
The verb vocabulary's hidden list names a key that is not a built-in verb; remove the entry.
A hidden built-in verb is named, also in a named signature's notBy or as a scenario step's response. Reported at the use; show the verb again, or name another verb.
A transition triggered by an event names a verb of its own: it takes its event's verb. Move the verb to the event when the event names none, or clear it.
An own verb's key equals a built-in verb's key once hyphens are dropped, such as setstate beside set-state; use the built-in verb.
A save changes the key of an own verb that is in use; rename it with the batch operation rename-verb, which rewrites every use.

A set's attribute is not one every subject of the process holds under one id: an unknown id, another entity's attribute, a to-one end, a collection or a value object's member; or the process has no subjects; or a context attribute named subject hides the object. Remove the set.
A set's attribute is derived, or holds a lifecycle's state (a bound attribute of this process or of any lifecycle that governs the subject), which only its chart moves. Remove the set.
One action, or one trigger point, sets one attribute twice. Remove the second set.

A rights entry is both an inline right and a use (right beside a key of an inline right) or neither (an inline right needs a name, an access and at least one verb); a use's right names something other than a named right; or an orchestration or a library has rights or rightsDefault, which only lifecycles hold. Remove the entry.
A right's states name something that is not a state of its lifecycle: another process's state, a history state or a choice state. Remove the state.

A right's ends are not ends every subject of its lifecycle holds, or stand beside a verb that cannot act on a link (any but connect, disconnect, read, modify, freeze and thaw); or its attributes are not attributes every subject of its lifecycle holds, or stand beside a verb other than read and modify or beside ends; a named right's are reported at each use. Remove the entry.

An allow right in a lifecycle that allows by default: each lifecycle answers on its own, so it cannot change any answer (a deny still wins over it, and without it the default allows). Remove it, or set the lifecycle's rightsDefault to deny.

Under rightsDefault deny, an event or a human task no one can ever do: it has no actors, its transitions no gate signers, and no allow right of its lifecycle names its verb (complete for a task); or an event with neither a verb nor actors nor signers. Add actors, or add an allow right.
An except entry that the same right's actors also names, so the right never applies to it. Remove it from except.
